thisWeek.title: Mindfulness
thisWeek.summary: This week is about noticing where my attention is and gently bringing it back, not trying to empty my mind or do mindfulness perfectly.

asks.text: Try Mindfulness of Breath and Body
Notice when my mind wanders and what helps bring it back

discussion: What did I notice about my wandering attention?
Did it help me switch off, read, relax or be more present?

values.name: Family
values.text: Protect and support the people I love without completely abandoning myself.

values.name: Home
values.text: A calm, safe and comfortable place that feels mine.

values.name: Peace
values.text: Protect sleep, rest, quiet and space from constant work or worry.

values.name: Freedom
values.text: Have parts of life that are mine, including hobbies, gliding, gardening and time outdoors.

values.name: Trust
values.text: Be reliable and trustworthy, while rebuilding trust in myself.

values.name: Kindness
values.text: Be caring and giving without turning that into self-sacrifice.

values.name: Contribution
values.text: Be useful, help others and give something back.

values.name: Health without obsession
values.text: Look after myself properly without letting health fear become the whole of life.

values.name: Living again
values.text: Move beyond survival mode and make room for things that make me feel like myself.

personal.text: Continue reading The Secret of Secrets
Put weedkiller on the brambles for Jason

principles.title: Notice avoidance
principles.text: If I hear 'I'll do it later', look for the smallest useful action rather than waiting to feel ready.

principles.title: Carrot, not stick
principles.text: Use what matters to me as motivation instead of giving myself shit.

principles.title: Good enough beats perfect
principles.text: Starting matters more than finding the perfect setup.

principles.title: Action before motivation
principles.text: I do not have to feel motivated first. Doing something can create momentum afterwards.

principles.title: Small chunks
principles.text: Long or mentally noisy tasks work better when I break them down.

principles.title: Be present
principles.text: Notice when my attention has wandered and bring it back to the person or activity in front of me.

sessions.title: Values and Bull's-Eye
sessions.ask: Read The Happiness Trap chapters 24-27, reflect on values and use the Bull's-Eye worksheet.
sessions.progress: Built a short values summary and completed the Bull's-Eye. The strongest direction was supporting family without completely abandoning myself, alongside home, peace, freedom, trust, kindness, contribution and living again.
sessions.source: Kirsty's email: Values, Questionnaires, and next session.

sessions.title: Goal setting
sessions.ask: Use the goal-setting matrix and Russ Harris SMART approach to create goals linked to values.
sessions.progress: Built a simple Love, Work, Play and Health grid. Reading, the 6pm work boundary and small practical actions became early goals.
sessions.next: Start acting on the goals and notice avoidance.

sessions.title: Behavioural Activation
sessions.ask: Follow the principles of Behavioural Activation; no need to fill in the whole pack.
sessions.progress: Used action before motivation, small achievable steps and honest avoidance tracking. Pleasure, achievement and connection became useful things to notice.
sessions.next: Keep building activity around values instead of waiting to feel motivated.

sessions.title: Presence and flash cards
sessions.ask: Practise carrot not stick, being present with others, enjoying food and finding the treasure in ordinary life.
sessions.progress: Reduced the homework to four simple things to notice rather than another large worksheet.
sessions.next: Practise noticing and presence during normal life rather than creating more jobs to complete.
sessions.source: Flash cards supplied after the Kirsty session.

sessions.title: Mindfulness
sessions.ask: Start with the Chocolate Meditation, Mindfulness of Breath and Body, and the 3-Minute Breathing Space.
sessions.progress: Current week. The aim is to try the exercises and notice what happens, not to do mindfulness perfectly.
sessions.next: Discuss which exercise was easiest or hardest and whether it helped with attention, reading, relaxing or switching off.

timeline.title: Major operation and recovery
timeline.text: A major turning point. Afterwards I did not feel fully like myself and life became heavily focused on survival, health and responsibility.

timeline.title: Bull's-Eye and goals

timeline.title: Acted against avoidance

timeline.title: Allotment and small steps

timeline.title: Behavioural Activation
timeline.text: Started using the idea that action can come before motivation, while noticing pleasure, achievement and connection.

timeline.title: Presence and flash cards
timeline.text: Focused on carrot not stick, being present, enjoying food and noticing ordinary good things.
